discovery: Programmable arrays of individually trapped neutral atoms interacting via Rydberg states for quantum simulation and quantum computation

nominees.name: Antoine Browaeys
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire Charles Fabry, Institut d'Optique Graduate School, CNRS, Université Paris-Saclay, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum information
motivation: The nominees turned single atoms held in optical tweezers into a controllable quantum many-body platform. Building on the Rydberg dipole-blockade proposal (Lukin and collaborators, 2001), Saffman and Browaeys demonstrated blockade between two individually trapped atoms (2009) and the first neutral-atom entangling gates. Browaeys then created defect-free, reconfigurable atom arrays in two and three dimensions. Lukin's group scaled these to hundreds of qubits, observed quantum phase transitions, many-body scars and topological spin liquids, and in 2023–2024 ran logical-qubit algorithms with error correction. This work started from careful atomic physics: laser cooling, trapping and coherent excitation of single atoms. It has become one of the leading routes to quantum simulation and fault-tolerant quantum computing. Laboratories worldwide now use these arrays to study problems in condensed-matter physics, high-energy physics and computation that were out of reach before. It is a fundamental advance in controlling quantum matter one atom at a time.
